3. Teamwork and Collaboration: Both members brainstormed ideas, shared knowledge and combined their creativity and skills. Inspired by the workshops, they applied what they learned, technology, problem-solving and teamwork to create their Space Exploration Simulator.
summary:
We developed Space Exploration Simulator, an interactive digital learning experience that takes users on a journey across the Moon, Mars and Space to explore NASA's space equipment left behind after their missions. Through interactive exploration, visual storytelling, images and mission information, young users can discover the machines that helped humanity explore other worlds.

The simulator brings the stories of NASA's discarded and retired space equipment to life. Users can explore selected rovers, landers, scientific instruments and landing components, learning why they were sent, what they were designed to do, what they achieved and the scientific discoveries they made possible. It transforms space mission history into an engaging and accessible experience for school-age learners.

Space exploration is not only about astronauts, rockets and successful landings. The machines left behind are also part of humanity's scientific and technological achievements. Their missions have contributed valuable knowledge about the Moon and Mars. By allowing young learners to explore these stories, our project encourages curiosity about space science, appreciation of engineering innovation and awareness of the legacy and responsibility of exploring other worlds.

Our message: Every mission leaves a legacy. Every discovery matters.
details:
Space Exploration Simulator

Space Exploration Simulator where space hardwares come alive telling their stories, science missios, purpose and current status through an interactive fun and engaging educational game.

Our project takes young space players on an exploration journey across three different environments: the Moon, Mars and Outer Space. In each environment, players discover NASA missions and spacecraft, learn about their functions and understand how different technologies help humans explore the universe.

The simulator features six real space exploration missions and spacecraft:

    • Apollo 12: The second successful crewed mission to land astronauts on the Moon. Players discover how astronauts explored the lunar surface and collected scientific samples.
    • Surveyor 3: An uncrewed lunar lander that investigated the Moon's surface and helped scientists understand its soil conditions before human exploration.
    • Opportunity Rover: A robotic rover that explored Mars, studied rocks and soil, and searched for evidence of past water activity.
    • Ingenuity Helicopter: The first helicopter to achieve powered, controlled flight on another planet, demonstrating new possibilities for aerial exploration on Mars.
    • Parker Solar Probe: A NASA spacecraft designed to study the Sun's outer atmosphere, known as the corona, helping scientists understand solar activity and space weather.
    • Voyager 2: A NASA spacecraft launched to explore the outer planets and now travelling through interstellar space, expanding our understanding of the distant universe.

Through interactive scenes, players can explore these missions, discover interesting space facts, understand how the equipment works and complete simple mission-based activities.

Benefits and Intended Impact

The project aims to make space science more accessible and enjoyable, especially for young learners. Instead of simply reading information from books or websites, players can actively explore different space environments and learn through interaction.

Our project provides several benefits:

  • Promotes STEM education: Introduces science, technology, engineering and mathematics through real-world space exploration examples.
  • Encourages curiosity: Inspires players to learn more about the Moon, Mars, the Sun and the wider universe.
  • Makes learning interactive: Transforms complex space science information into simple, engaging activities.
  • Develops problem-solving skills: Encourages players to think, explore and complete mission-based challenges.
  • Raises awareness of space exploration: Helps players appreciate the importance of scientific research and technological innovation.

Our intended impact is to inspire the next generation of space enthusiasts, scientists, engineers and explorers by making learning about space exciting and meaningful.

Tools, Coding Languages and Software

The project is developed using mBlock, a visual programming platform that uses block-based coding to make programming easier and more accessible.

We use mBlock programming blocks to create interactive animations, characters, backgrounds, buttons, dialogue, scene transitions and mission activities. These programming elements allow players to navigate between the Moon, Mars and Outer Space exploration sections and interact with different spacecraft and equipment.

We also incorporate digital illustrations, animations and information based on real NASA space missions to make the learning experience more informative and engaging.

Creativity and Innovation

The creative aspect of our project is the combination of space education and interactive gaming. We transform real space exploration missions into an interactive simulator where players can discover how different spacecraft and technologies operate in different space environments.

By organising the simulator into three exploration destinations, each featuring two selected spacecraft or missions, we create a journey that introduces players to different aspects of space exploration.

From human lunar exploration and robotic Mars missions to studying the Sun and travelling beyond our solar system, the project demonstrates the diversity of space exploration technologies.

By combining storytelling, animations, interactive elements and educational challenges, we aim to make space science interesting and easier to understand for young audiences.

Factors Considered During Development

While developing our project, our team considered several important factors:

  1. Educational accuracy: We refer to real NASA missions and spacecraft information to ensure that the content is informative and fact-based.
  2. Target audience: We aim to make the simulator suitable for young learners through simple language, colourful visuals and easy-to-understand activities.
  3. User experience: We design clear instructions, simple controls and interactive features so that players can navigate the simulator easily.
  4. Creativity and engagement: We incorporate animations, storytelling, mission challenges and interactive elements to maintain players' interest.
  5. Technical feasibility: We consider the capabilities of mBlock and ensure that the project can run smoothly while delivering an enjoyable experience.
  6. Learning value: Every exploration destination and activity is designed to provide meaningful knowledge about space exploration rather than being purely entertainment.

Through this project, we hope to demonstrate that learning about space does not have to be complicated. With creativity, technology and interactive storytelling, we can bring the wonders of space exploration closer to everyone.
